title: Derivation of Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation under Gravity
governing_principles: Momentum balance of system (rocket + ejected mass dm) in ground inertial frame
assumptions: Constant exhaust speed u_ex relative to rocket nozzle

derivation_steps.description: At time t, the rocket has mass m and vertical upward velocity v, with linear momentum P(t).
At time t + dt, rocket mass is m + dm (where dm < 0), velocity is v + dv, and expelled gas mass -dm travels at v - u_ex.

derivation_steps.equation: dP = P(t + dt) - P(t) = m dv + u_{\text{ex}} dm + dm dv \approx m dv + u_{\text{ex}} dm
derivation_steps.description: Subtract P(t) and neglect the second-order differential dm dv.

derivation_steps.equation: dP = F_{\text{ext}} dt = -m g \, dt \implies m dv + u_{\text{ex}} dm = -m g \, dt
derivation_steps.description: Equate the momentum change to external gravitational impulse dP = -mg dt.
Divide through by instantaneous rocket mass m to separate variables.

derivation_steps.equation: \int_{v_0}^v dv = -u_{\text{ex}} \int_{m_0}^m \frac{dm}{m} - g \int_0^t dt \implies v - v_0 = -u_{\text{ex}} \ln\left(\frac{m}{m_0}\right) - gt = u_{\text{ex}} \ln\left(\frac{m_0}{m}\right) - gt
derivation_steps.description: Integrate from launch state (v0, m0, t=0) to instantaneous state (v, m, t) to obtain Tsiolkovsky equation.

limiting_cases: Zero gravity (g = 0): v = v0 + u_ex ln(m0/m) (ideal deep-space rocket equation).
Zero mass ejected (m = m0): v = v0 - gt (standard ballistic free fall).
dimensional_check: u_ex ln(m0/m) has units of speed [L][T]^-1, and gt has units of speed [L][T]^-1.
source_provenance: HCV1 Ch 9 pp. 161-163; HRW Ch 9 pp. 254-256; UP Ch 8 pp. 290-291
